title: Benchmarking Ethernet Interconnect for HPC/AI workloads
problem: Ethernet interconnects need to match InfiniBand's performance to provide cost-effective, open-standard solutions for HPC and AI workloads. This paper benchmarks 100G and 200G Ethernet systems to evaluate their bandwidth and latency characteristics versus InfiniBand.
motivation: Industry requires high-performance, cost-effective Ethernet solutions with competitive latency to enable modern AI workloads while maintaining open standards.
method: Two HPC systems using 100G and 200G Ethernet interconnects are benchmarked and directly compared against InfiniBand. Performance metrics including bandwidth and latency are measured across message sizes, with emphasis on large message exchange scenarios.
key_novelty: Empirical demonstration that modern Ethernet interconnects (100G/200G) achieve competitive performance parity with InfiniBand, particularly for large message exchanges.
contributions: Benchmarking of 100G and 200G Ethernet interconnect performance for HPC systems
Comparative analysis showing Ethernet competitive performance versus InfiniBand
Evidence supporting Ethernet viability for large message exchanges in AI workloads
Validation of open-standard Ethernet as viable alternative for high-performance interconnects
limitations: Paper presents preliminary findings from early systems; scalability assessment, diverse workload coverage, and practical deployment considerations not discussed.
primary_theme: Ethernet interconnect performance benchmarking for HPC/AI
